methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Standard Subsea is a Seed-stage frontier-tech company in Ocean & Maritime founded by Christopher Amidon. The company has raised $10M+ to date. The comparable universe consists of three private peers in the sector (Clippership, NetworkOcean, Albacore); no public comparables exist in this nascent segment.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which is the applicable triangulation method given data availability constraints. Using total capital raised of $10M as a proxy for post-money valuation at Seed close, a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to Series A entry yields an implied valuation of $25M. This reflects observed market practice for early-stage advancement in emerging maritime technology without requiring public market multiples or revenue-based metrics.

The triangulated range spans $21M (low) to $29M (high), with a median point estimate of $25M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single methodology rather than consensus across multiple approaches. Key uncertainties include the absence of public comparables to benchmark sector multiples, limited visibility into the private peer set's financials and growth trajectories, and the early-stage nature of the company, which typically correlates with higher valuation volatility. Any refined analysis would benefit from access to metrics on the three identified private peers and forward-looking revenue or unit economics for Standard Subsea itself.
